summary: Worker A: preparation-specific thyme microwave oil and polar solvent extracts; measured study-specific rosmarinic acid; negative and positive in-vitro bacterial assays; verified thymol PubChem identity. No therapeutic inference. Pending publisher unblock due replayed batch 002.
research_method: Direct review of Gedikoglu et al. (2019) tables 1, 4, 5 and methods; PubChem thymol identity. Two technical replicates in the 2019 study. No extrapolation to other chemotypes, human efficacy or safe dose.

sources.title: Thymol, CID 6989, compound structure and chemical identifiers
sources.organization: PubChem, U.S. National Library of Medicine

structures.binding_warning: Compound identity and structure do not establish binding, clinical benefit, bioavailability or safety.

medicinal_materials.part: Air-dried cultivated Thymus vulgaris aerial material (Diyarbakir Research Institute, July 2017)
medicinal_materials.preparation: Microwave-assisted essential oil fraction (MAE), analytical research sample
medicinal_materials.processing: Reported oil yield 1.77 ± 0.05% w/w (n=2); thymol 50.53% and p-cymene 11.79% reported as relative GC-MS peak area. This method did not significantly change oil yield versus hydrodistillation in this sample.
medicinal_materials.limitations: Study-specific oil and batch. Relative GC-MS peak area is not mass fraction or purity. Not a clinical product, safe dose or general species yield.

medicinal_materials.preparation: Laboratory 80% aqueous methanol polar extract, subsequently freeze-dried
medicinal_materials.processing: Study-reported rosmarinic acid value 13.66 ± 0.145% in Table 4; total phenolics 15.13 ± 0.313 mg gallic-acid equivalents/g dry weight; DPPH IC50 29.22 ± 0.385 µg/mL (n=2).
medicinal_materials.limitations: Methanol is a laboratory solvent; no suggestion for home use or consumption. Table 4 reported composition percentages are study-method-specific and not purified rosmarinic acid yield or safe dose. Cell-free antioxidant results do not prove human benefit.

medicinal_materials.preparation: Laboratory 80% aqueous ethanol polar extract, subsequently freeze-dried
medicinal_materials.processing: Study-reported rosmarinic acid value 8.696 ± 0.055% in Table 4; total phenolics 13.57 ± 0.103 mg gallic-acid equivalents/g dry weight; DPPH IC50 36.77 ± 0.45 µg/mL (n=2).
medicinal_materials.limitations: Research extraction with solvent removal and analysis, not an ingestible preparation or dosing guidance. Percent values are method/sample-specific and do not establish purified compound yield or clinical activity.

occurrences.plant_part: Dried cultivated herb, polar laboratory extracts
occurrences.note: HPLC-determined rosmarinic acid: Table 4 reported 13.66 ± 0.145% in 80% methanol extract and 8.696 ± 0.055% in 80% ethanol extract (n=2). Reported percentages are analytical extract composition, not an organism-wide concentration or pure isolate yield. No clinical efficacy inference.

bioactivities.target_taxon: Bacillus cereus NRRL B3711; Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 9144; Staphylococcus epidermidis ATCC 12228; Escherichia coli ATCC 25922; Salmonella enteritidis ATCC 13076; Salmonella typhimurium ATCC 14028
bioactivities.study_model: In-vitro disk diffusion, 80% methanol and 80% ethanol extracts from cultivated thyme (Gedikoglu et al. 2019)
bioactivities.endpoint: Growth inhibition zone in six bacterial cultures
bioactivities.observed_effect: Neither polar extract displayed detectable antibacterial activity against the six tested strains under the reported disk diffusion conditions.
bioactivities.mechanism_status: Not determined; negative in this assay does not establish absence of all antimicrobial activity.
bioactivities.dose_translation: No clinical efficacy, dose, or antimicrobial-treatment inference.
bioactivities.limitations: One laboratory study with n=2; extract type and diffusion behavior matter. Not a universal negative finding for all thyme extracts, microbes, concentrations or conditions.

bioactivities.study_model: In-vitro disk diffusion of hydrodistilled vs microwave-assisted thyme essential oils, n=2 (Gedikoglu et al. 2019)
bioactivities.observed_effect: Hydrodistilled oil 24.5 ± 2.96 mm; microwave-assisted oil 29 ± 2.24 mm for S. aureus ATCC 9144 (Table 5).
bioactivities.mechanism_status: Oil mixture tested; no individual thymol target-binding or mechanistic attribution established.
bioactivities.dose_translation: In-vitro inhibition zones cannot be translated into human antimicrobial treatment or safe ingestion.
bioactivities.limitations: Specific strain, preparation and disk-diffusion conditions only, n=2. Relative peak-area composition is not purity; no animal/human outcomes.
